1.why: Every screen is a static, clean card layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary actions use high-contrast dark-blue buttons and clear headings that stand out from the pale background.

3.why: Each step presents a single focused form so the needed field and button are immediately visible.

4.why: The user must remember and manually transfer a long recovery token and later an MFA code across multiple distinct steps.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill affordances, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: Apart from the email field retaining its value on step 2, there are no visual cues for previously saved or familiar items.

7.why: Labels and instructions are short, plain-language sentences with good contrast.

8.why: No error states or corrective error messages are shown in any of the eight screenshots.

9.why: Password rules are stated but no example values or formatted illustrations of what to type are provided.

10.why: The flow offers only password + MFA code; no alternative methods such as face or code-app login are presented.

11.why: Each screen contains at most one input field and one primary button, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Green confirmation text, log entries, and the final “appointment request has been confirmed” message clearly state outcomes.

13.why: Occasional static notes appear, yet there are no contextual tips or progressive help for new steps.

14.why: Forms remain editable so a user can re-enter data, but no explicit “try again” guidance or undo is shown.

15.why: Header, card layout, button style and log panel remain identical across all eight steps, supporting consistent learning.
